speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of your eyes and skin; this suggests jaundice. To understand the severity and cause, please tell me exactly how old you are in hours and if your stool has become pale or clay-colored, or if your urine is dark.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding-associated jaundice. The infant is 2 weeks old, exclusively breastfed, and has increasing jaundice, which typically resolves by this age if due to dehydration or insufficient intake; however, I must rule out pathologic causes like biliary atresia (pale stools) or hemolysis. REQUEST TEST: Total and Direct Bilirubin. REQUEST TEST: Blood Type and Coombs Test. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.
